title: Machine Learning Engineer, Public Sector
text:
The goal of a Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to leverage techniques in the fields of generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI to improve Scale's products and customer experience in production environments. Our machine learning engineers take advantage of robust internal infrastructure and  unique access to massive datasets to deliver improvements to our customers.
 Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like   Donovan and  Thunderforge . Our work spans multiple modalities, with a strong focus on both large language models and computer vision. On the LLM side, we are developing agentic systems that help solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners. This includes building agent frameworks that integrate with custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, as well as evaluation tools to benchmark and refine agent behavior. We're also advancing research in areas like reinforcement learning for agentic LLMs, with successful deployment into real-world operational environments. On the computer vision front, we're training advanced models to increase labeling throughput and automate perception tasks. Our efforts include building large-scale fine-tuning pipelines, training models across multiple modalities, and developing generalizable vision foundation models to support a wide range of defense applications.
 You will: 
- Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community, use them in production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
- Improve and maintain production models through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
- Collaborate with product and research teams to identify and prototype ML-driven product enhancements, including for upcoming product lines
- Work with massive datasets to develop both generic models as well as fine tune models for specific products
- Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
- Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
- Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs
 This role will require an active TS security clearance  
 Ideally You’d Have: 
- 2+  years  of experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production environments
- Extensive experience with GenAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning, or computer vision in a production environment
- Solid background in algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming
- Strong programming skills in Python, experience in Tensorflow or PyTorch
 Nice to Haves: 
- Experience deploying software into environments you can't reach from your laptop - on-prem, edge, air-gapped, or otherwise restricted networks. Regulated industries count; the constraint is the point, not the sector.
- Any prior exposure to government or defense work: military or civilian service, a cleared internship, or time at a federal contractor.
- Hands-on fine-tuning of open-weight models - LoRA/PEFT, instruction tuning, or training embedding models, at work or on your own.
- Having written evaluations for a system whose output isn't deterministic: benchmarks, LLM judges, or a regression suite that caught something real.
- Experience with geospatial data or maps - GIS tooling, spatial reference systems, or imagery.
- A shipped project with real users behind it, where you owned it after launch rather than handing it off at merge.

title: Frontier Data Strategist
text:
Frontier AI labs decide what direction their models need to take before the actual training starts. As a Frontier Data Strategist on Scale's Generative AI team, you'll be a trusted voice in those decisions. You'll partner with research leads and senior stakeholders at the world's leading AI labs to shape the data strategy behind their next generation of models, then design the human-data programs to deliver it.
 You'll sit where frontier research meets Scale's product roadmap, and you'll be expected to move both. With customers, you'll own senior, technically grounded relationships, anticipate where their research is heading, and bring them new data ideas before they ask. Inside Scale, you'll be a leading voice with our AI Product Managers, ML Research, Delivery Operations, and Engagement Management teams, turning what you learn from customers into product priorities and investment decisions.
 This is a forward-looking, highly cross-functional role. Our Engagement Managers own customer success for live programs; Frontier Data Strategists own everything that comes before it: spotting the need, designing the program, scoping and forecasting it, and winning the work. As a senior member of the team, you'll set the standard for how Scale does this work and help develop the Frontier Data Strategists around you.
 What you’ll do: 
- Own relationships with senior research stakeholders at your assigned frontier labs, such as research leads, heads of post-training, and technical leadership, and become a strategic thought partner on their post-training, evaluation, and agent roadmaps.
- Set the data strategy for your accounts: anticipate needs across research areas, spot where the biggest opportunities are, and build a multi-program plan for how Scale can help.
- Direct the cross-functional team designing Scale's most complex and novel human-data programs, including work that has no precedent at Scale.
- Shape Scale's product roadmap by representing your customers in planning with AI Product Managers and ML Research, and by resolving tradeoffs between customer needs and what Scale can build.
- Bring insights from the frontier (research directions, emerging data needs, capability gaps) back to Scale's leadership and technical teams to guide strategy and investment decisions.
- Own the pipeline of new opportunities for your accounts. Lead scoping, forecasting, and pricing with Delivery, Growth Operations, and Finance, and see the work through to signed programs and a clean handoff.
- Mentor Frontier Data Strategists, set the bar for program design and customer engagement, and help build the playbooks the team runs on.
 What we’re looking for:  
- 3+ years in a technical AI/ML role, such as ML engineering, research, applied science, technical product management, or post-training data work at a lab or data provider.
- Deep fluency in the LLM training lifecycle, especially post-training: SFT, preference data, reward modeling, RL environments, evaluations, agentic training, etc.
- A track record of owning relationships with senior technical stakeholders, and of influencing their direction through substance.
- Evidence of shipping ambiguous, high-stakes technical programs from idea to delivery.
- Experience influencing a product or research roadmap without direct authority.
- The ability to read a research paper and form an opinion on what data would improve a given capability, and to defend that opinion to researchers.
- A degree in CS, engineering, math, physics, or another quantitative field.
 Ideally you'd have: 
- Hands-on experience designing training data, evals, or RL environments.
- A graduate degree (PhD, MS) or published research in ML or a related field.
- Experience at a frontier lab, model developer, or AI data company.
- Experience mentoring or leading technical teammates, formally or informally.
- A background in founding or leading at an early-stage startup, or in pre-sales, solutions engineering, or technical consulting.

title: Legal Fellow - Human Frontier Collective (US, UK, & Canada)
text:
PLEASE NOTE: This is a fully remote, 1099 independent contractor opportunity with an estimated duration of six months and the potential for extension. This role is open to candidates residing in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada.To be eligible, candidates must be authorized to work in the country they reside in.  
 About the Program 
 The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) Fellowship brings together top researchers and domain experts to collaborate on high-impact work that are shaping the future of AI. As an HFC Fellow, you’ll apply your academic and professional expertise to help design, evaluate, and interpret advanced generative AI systems—while gaining exposure to cutting-edge research and working alongside an interdisciplinary network of leading thinkers.
 What You'll Do 
- Collaborative Work: Get invited to engage in high-impact projects with our partnered AI labs and platforms. Design complex real-world scenarios, evaluating model outputs for accuracy and regulatory alignment, and providing targeted feedback to improve performance across domains like compliance, litigation, case law, and contract analysis.
- HFC Community: Beyond the work, you’ll become part of a supportive, interdisciplinary network of innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI across domains.
- Contribute to Research Publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition (e.g., SciPredict , PropensityBench , Professional Reasoning Benchmark ).
 Who Should Apply 
- Education: JD, LLM, or currently enrolled in a prestigious 2L/3L program. 
- Certifications: Bar admission in any jurisdiction strongly preferred.
- Professional Background: Experience as Attorney/Associate, Legal Analyst, Counsel, Law Clerk, In-House Counsel, Legal Researcher, or Law Professor. 
- Skills: Demonstrated expertise in legal research, analysis of regulatory frameworks, constitutional law, case law interpretation, and drafting legal briefs.
- Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion for financial technology and a commitment to collaboration. Prior experience with AI is not required, but a plus.
 Why Join the HFC? 
- Advance Legal AI Solutions: Apply your legal expertise to address complex, real-world challenges where your judgment shapes advanced AI reasoning and supports critical legal decision-making.
- Professional Development: High-impact legal experts expand their influence through review projects, advisory roles, and research—while deepening their AI expertise, sharpening legal analysis skills, and gaining practical experience with innovative AI tools for the legal field.
- Join a Top-Tier Network: Collaborate with a global network of academics and experts to advance responsible AI through impactful, flexible research and training. 80% of our members come from leading institutions.
- Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule, with flexible 10–40 hour weeks that fit around your life and other commitments.
- Competitive Pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and are depending on a number of factors, including but not limited to; projects, scope, skillset, and location. 
 Application Process 
- Apply: We review applications on a rolling basis.
- Complete a Challenge: Selected candidates will undertake a brief task designed to reflect HFC work and evaluate their domain expertise.
- Interview: Candidates will get to discuss their research experience, professional background, and alignment with our mission to advance human-centered AI.
- Join the Collective: Successful candidates will receive an invitation to join the Human Frontier Collective Fellowship.

title: Technical Writer
text:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
As a technical writer and editor, you’ll play a key role in helping our customers succeed by creating, maintaining, and improving documentation that supports users of Palantir’s products.
 
At Palantir, we view documentation as a key part of product development. Working at the intersection of users and Palantir’s products, you will develop an understanding of user needs and help them get the most out of our software. You’ll be a thought partner with our product development teams, combining your communication skills with empathy for users and product knowledge. Your work will primarily be on written documentation, but may also include interactive tutorials, recorded demonstrations, or other communication channels.
 
Teams and individuals at Palantir operate with a high degree of autonomy and independence. In this role, you’ll be responsible for setting priorities for your work, deciding where to allocate your time based on an assessment of stakeholder and organizational needs. You should be comfortable thinking about the “big picture” narrative and structure of our documentation, as well as diving into the details. On any given day, you might find yourself editing a guide drafted by a developer, writing a new tutorial for a critical workflow, or identifying an area that needs improvement and partnering with a team to make the fix. You will also gain exposure to the technical infrastructure for composing and distributing platform documentation.

Core Responsibilities
- Understand and communicate the value proposition of Palantir’s products.
- Create user documentation in partnership with developers and business teams.
- Review and edit documentation to maintain a high level of quality.
- Identify, triage, and resolve needs in documentation.
- Maintain style guides and best practices for writing, improving, and publishing documentation.
- Manage and structure multi-stakeholder documentation projects.
- Uphold a culture in which developers are engaged with documenting their products, including hosting training sessions and workshops.
What We Value
- Commitment to quality and accuracy in communication and writing, with the ability to translate complex technical subjects into clear, concise prose suited for the intended audience.
- Ability to prioritize, adapt, and operate in unstructured environments as part of a fast-moving team.
- Enthusiasm for learning about and communicating new technology and concepts.
- Experience working with engineering teams as part of the software development process.
What We Require
- Outstanding writing and editing skills.
- 3+ years of technical writing experience or similar experience in software development.
- Experience with programming, scripting, or statistical packages; previous work in software engineering or data science is a plus.
Salary
 
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $88,000 - $122,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.


Our benefits aim to promote health and wellbeing across all areas of Palantirians’ lives. We work to continuously improve our offerings and listen to our community as we design and update them. The list below details our available benefits and some of the perks that can be enjoyed as an employee of Palantir Technologies.
 
Benefits
 
•  Employees (and their eligible dependents) can enroll in medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as voluntary life insurance
•  Employees are automatically covered by Palantir’s basic life, AD&D and disability insurance
•  Commuter benefits
•  Relocation assistance
•  Take what you need paid time off, not accrual based
•  2 weeks paid time off built into the end of each year (subject to team and business needs)
•  10 paid holidays throughout the calendar year
•  Supportive leave of absence program including time off for military service and medical events
•  Paid leave for new parents and subsidized back-up care for all parents
•  Fertility and family building benefits including but not limited to adoption, surrogacy, and preservation
•  Stipend to help with expenses that come with a new child
•  Employees can enroll in Palantir’s 401k plan
 
Life at Palantir
 
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. The Role
 
Palantir’s software forms the operating system for the militaries of the United States and her allies, driving outcomes and enhancing capabilities across the full spectrum of operations, intelligence, and support activities. Our defense applications are the tip of that spear, powerful tools used daily by thousands of soldiers, sailors, airmen, and marines to perform critical work at home and abroad from the Pentagon to the front lines. The engineers who build, maintain, and extend these applications are responsible for wielding the immense technical potential of Palantir’s data modeling and AI platforms to create exquisite domain-specific workflows and interfaces that modernize, extend, and revolutionize the capabilities of the warfighter.
 
This is a front-end engineering role focused on marrying Palantir’s Foundry and AIP platform technologies, application specific backend services, and modern web technologies with domain expertise. These teams are nimble and select the right tool for the task in front of them rather than adhering to a rigidly defined tech stack, but the most common setups are React for standard DOM rendering, Maplibre and/or Three js for geospatial and 3D rendering, Redux (in various flavors) for state management, Conjure for API management, and OSDK for interaction with the foundry platform. A rich ecosystem of in-house libraries and toolchains sit on top of that foundation to provide cross-app messaging, live data streaming, robust classification based access control, and a host of other specialized functions. Defense applications developers both consume and produce these re-usable tools as part of their core engineering role.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As an engineer on a defense application team you’ll be responsible for owning, not just executing, user-facing feature additions or enhancements. Defense product teams are forward-leaning by nature, you can expect to spend time hands-on with customers and forward-deployed engineers to design solutions that not only meet the need but deliver value rapidly to support customers in ever-changing environments. The dynamic nature of the defense applications teams make for, on average, shorter project cycles with high ownership at the individual contributor level but demand flexibility, practicality, and responsibility.
 
The highly autonomous nature of teams means you will transition from mentee to mentor quickly as you build unique expertise in specific applications and features. Palantir’s engineering culture puts a premium on everyone having the skills and willingness to teach and learn, regardless of tenure. The best Palantir engineers form strong convictions quickly (to avoid analysis paralysis when every day counts) but hold them weakly, always ready to revise their opinion and update their world view when new ideas or additional data points are presented.

- Autodidacticism : we push boundaries and are constantly reinventing ourselves, you’ll never stop learning new things.
- Collaboration : These are small teams solving hard problems, it only works when we pool our abilities and play off each person’s strengths.
- Creativityand problem solving : You’ll be given objectives and goals, not blueprints and instructions.
- Dependability : Palantir’s engineering culture is built on a foundation of trust and requires ever developer to own their own outcomes and communicate proactively when confronted with the unexpected.

- 2+ years of frontend software engineering experience
- Strong frontend coding skills: regardless of which frameworks you use or how you learned them, we're looking for people who can write clean, effective code with proficiency in JavaScript and an understanding of how web technologies work
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent understanding of algorithms, performance, and systems design

What We're About
 
At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.
 
If you believe in the transformational power of data and technology and in your own ability to bring that power to bear against complex problems, we want to meet you.
 
What We Do
 
As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most challenging problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.
 
Deployment Strategists are do-ers who immerse themselves in our customers' most intricate workflows, partner with customer teams and explore the data, and dive into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll tackle will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user empathy to ultimately empower our customers to make better decisions.

No two days are the same, but as a Deployment Strategist you can expect to:
- Go onsite and meet with customer analysts to understand the critical questions they need to answer and locate their biggest pain points.
- Identify relevant datasets through deep engagement with customer problems and workflows, and work with Forward Deployed Engineers to integrate the data into a stable and extensible pipeline.
- Work with the customer to build bespoke workflows for new user groups.
- Lead training sessions to ensure that the product is meeting user needs, and to ensure it is being used widely enough to have concrete impact on our partners' operations.
- Present the results of our work and proposals for future work to audiences ranging from analysts to C-suite executives.
- Embed with our Software Engineering and Product Design teams to incorporate what you saw in the field into cross-Palantir product offerings.
- Build and deliver demos to new and existing customers.
- Scope out potential engagements in new industries and in increasingly expanding locations around the world.
What We Value
- We value team members who aren’t satisfied with surface-level answers. We value the desire to dive into the details of the data because that’s the core of our work. And we value low ego because the outcome matters more than who gets the credit.
- Extraordinary ability to take on open-ended problems in unstructured environments.
- Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow.
- Ability to travel 25 – 75% required. Varies by location and team.
- Experience with programming, scripting or statistical packages (e.g. Python, R, Matlab, SQL) is a plus.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer - AUS Government
text:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open ended question like “Why are we delaying so many flights?” or “How can we better identify instances of money laundering?” As an FDSE, you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.

As an FDSE your responsibilities look similar to those of a startup CTO: you’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.

Whether you aspire to be an entrepreneur or an engineering leader, we believe Palantir is the best place — with the best colleagues — to learn how. You’ll learn how to unpack a problem and understand the costs and consequences of its solution. You’ll learn new technologies and languages, and even develop them yourself. You’ll work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop.

Our Principles
- Impact: We take on meaningful and challenging projects that change the world for the better.
- Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter.
- Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on-site, to understand and solve their problems.
- Trust: We trust each other to effectively manage time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves.
- Growth: We encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge.
- Learning: We often face entirely novel problems where we need to pick up a lot of new knowledge and learn how to use it to make progress. We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers.
What We Value
- Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Data Science.

text:

Palantir's defense product vertical builds mission-critical products for the modern warfighter, enabling them to securely integrate and visualize their data, perform rich analyses, and build sophisticated, full-fledged programs such as common operating pictures, alert-triaging inboxes, and resource allocation planning tools driven by rich-ML models. Our customers use our defense offering to drive core operations within their organizations - these programs are relied upon for daily operations in the command centers and battlefronts of militaries across the world.
 
Palantir's Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds geospatial mapping tools for mission critical operations, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different aspects of each product.

Firma, która zmienia świat

W Palantirze dążymy do rozwiązywania najważniejszych i najbardziej wymagających problemów na świecie. Wierzymy, że tworzenie oprogramowania umożliwiającego podejmowanie decyzji przez ludzi jest najlepszym sposobem na osiągnięcie tego celu. Współpracujemy z najważniejszymi instytucjami na świecie, aby przeobrazić sposób, w jaki wykorzystują dane i technologię. Nasze oprogramowanie było wykorzystywane m.in. do powstrzymania ataków terrorystycznych, odkrywania nowych leków, zdobywania przewagi na globalnych rynkach finansowych.

Rola

Jako analityk ds. niezawodności systemów i operacji jesteś siłą napędową wdrożeń rozwiązań Palantir. Odpowiadasz za opracowywanie, wdrażanie i realizację procesów, które usprawniają przepływ pracy i ograniczają utrudnienia. Monitorujesz projekty i dbasz o ich stabilny przebieg, usuwasz przeszkody oraz przewidujesz potrzeby klientów, aby nasi inżynierowie mogli skupić się na rozwiązywaniu problemów technicznych, do których są najlepiej przygotowani.

Na tym stanowisku potrzebne są umiejętności zarządzania projektami, optymalizacji procesów i skutecznej realizacji zadań. Lubisz rozwiązywać problemy i zawsze stawiasz na najlepszy pomysł, nawet jeśli nie jest Twój.

Podstawowe obowiązki
Zajmuj się różnorodnymi problemami i wyzwaniami. Jednego dnia możesz wspierać wdrożenie u dużego klienta o globalnym zasięgu, a już następnego lecieć na drugi koniec świata, aby pomóc przy nowym projekcie pilotażowym.
Bądź jedną z pierwszych osób, które reagują, gdy pojawiają się problemy. Nawet jeśli problem wykracza poza obszar Twojej specjalizacji, podejmujesz inicjatywę, by go rozwiązać, i prosisz o pomoc dopiero wtedy, gdy wyczerpiemy wszystkie dostępne nam możliwości.
Opracowuj i wdrażaj procesy, które ograniczają utrudnienia i pozwalają wszystkim członkom zespołu skupić się na tym, co robią najlepiej.
Myśl kreatywnie, współpracuj i rób wszystko, aby wykonać zadanie.
Co sobie cenimy
Wyjątkowa umiejętność podejmowania trafnych decyzji i zachowania spokoju pod dużą presją.
Kreatywne podejście do zarządzania projektami oparte na prostych i elastycznych metodykach, które umożliwiają szybkie wprowadzanie kolejnych zmian i bieżące informowanie klientów o postępach bez zbędnych formalności.
Udokumentowane sukcesy w budowaniu owocnych relacji z klientami opartych na współpracy.
Skrupulatna dbałość o szczegóły, w tym prowadzenie dokładnej dokumentacji i staranne śledzenie kluczowych wskaźników projektu.
Zaangażowanie w pracę na miejscu u klientów i/lub we wspieranie projektów wewnętrznych oraz kadry kierowniczej wyższego szczebla, połączone z umiejętnością wprowadzania ładu i usprawniania kluczowych inicjatyw wewnętrznych.
Wymagania
Gotowość do podróży służbowych obejmujących 25–75% czasu pracy (w zależności od lokalizacji i zespołu).
Co najmniej 3 lata doświadczenia w zarządzaniu projektami lub programami, najlepiej w dynamicznym środowisku o szybkim tempie pracy.
Gotowość do pracy stacjonarnej w naszej lokalizacji (lokalizacjach) w Warszawie przez pięć dni w tygodniu.
Biegła znajomość języka polskiego.

Życie w Palantir

Chcemy, aby każdy z pracowników firmy Palantir osiągał najlepsze wyniki, dlatego doceniamy mocne strony, umiejętności i zainteresowania poszczególnych osób od pierwszej rozmowy kwalifikacyjnej po długoterminowy rozwój, zamiast polegać na tradycyjnych drabinach kariery. Zwracanie uwagi na potrzeby naszej społeczności umożliwia nam optymalizację naszych możliwości rozwoju i pomaga zapewnić wiele dróg do sukcesu w Palantir. Promowanie zdrowia i dobrego samopoczucia we wszystkich obszarach życia pracowników firmy Palantir to tylko jeden ze sposobów inwestowania w naszą społeczność. Dowiedz się więcej na stronie Życie w Palantir i pamiętaj, że nasza oferta może się różnić w zależności od regionu.

Wierzymy, że postępowanie zgodne z wartościami i kulturą firmy Palantir sprawia, iż pracownicy „lepiej współpracują ze sobą”, a praca osobista daje możliwość bardziej kreatywnych wyników. Dlatego zachęcamy pracowników do pracy w naszych biurach, aby wspierać powiązania i innowacje. Wiele zespołów oferuje opcje hybrydowe (dzień lub dwa dni w tygodniu pracy w domu), dzięki czemu nasi pracownicy mogą uzyskać odpowiedni kompromis dla swojej osobistej produktywności. W zależności od potrzeb biznesowych istnieje kilka ról, które pozwalają na „zdalną” pracę w wyjątkowych warunkach. Jeśli ubiegasz się o jedno z tych stanowisk, musisz pracować w mieście i kraju, w którym jesteś zatrudniony. Jeśli oferta w ogłoszeniu jest określona jako „na miejscu”, musisz pracować w biurze.

Jeśli chcesz wzmacniać najważniejsze instytucje świata, jest to miejsce dla Ciebie. Palantir ceni doskonałość niezależnie od pochodzenia. Dokładamy wszelkich starań, aby proces składania aplikacji i zatrudniania był dostępny dla wszystkich, oraz zapewnimy odpowiednie udogodnienia osobom z niepełnosprawnością. Jeśli potrzebujesz udogodnienia w procesie aplikacji lub zatrudnienia, skontaktuj się z nami i daj nam znać, jak możemy Ci pomóc.

Pamiętaj, że nigdy nie zostaniesz poproszony(-a) o przesłanie płatności lub udostępnienie informacji finansowych w celu wzięcia udziału w naszym procesie rekrutacyjnym. text:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


What We're About
 
At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.
 
If you believe in the transformational power of data and technology and in your own ability to bring that power to bear against complex problems, we want to meet you.
 
What We Do
 
As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most challenging problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.
 
Deployment Strategists are do-ers who immerse themselves in our customers' most intricate workflows, partner with customer teams and explore the data, and dive into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll tackle will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user empathy to ultimately empower our customers to make better decisions.

No two days are the same, but as a Deployment Strategist you can expect to:
- Go onsite and meet with customer analysts to understand the critical questions they need to answer and locate their biggest pain points.
- Identify relevant datasets through deep engagement with customer problems and workflows, and work with Forward Deployed Engineers to integrate the data into a stable and extensible pipeline.
- Work with the customer to build bespoke workflows for new user groups.
- Lead training sessions to ensure that the product is meeting user needs, and to ensure it is being used widely enough to have concrete impact on our partners' operations.
- Present the results of our work and proposals for future work to audiences ranging from analysts to C-suite executives.
- Embed with our Software Engineering and Product Design teams to incorporate what you saw in the field into cross-Palantir product offerings.
- Build and deliver demos to new and existing customers.
- Scope out potential engagements in new industries and in increasingly expanding locations around the world.
What We Value
- Team members who aren’t satisfied with surface-level answers and will dive into the details of the data.
- Extraordinary ability to take on open-ended problems in unstructured environments.
- Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow.
- Ability to travel 25 – 75% required. Varies by location and team.
- Experience with programming, scripting or statistical packages (e.g. Python, R, Matlab, SQL) is a plus.

title: Product Designer, New Grad - US Government
text:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
The Palantir Design Team is responsible for the human experience of using our software. Our team is growing rapidly, but we're committed to creating a tight-knit team environment that fosters trust, integrity, empathy, and growth. We work together in realizing a shared product vision, and regularly give feedback and critique to each other.

Designing at Palantir is a varied experience. On a given day, you might be: leading a design sprint for your product team; designing a micro-interaction to make a complex analytical task feel simple; and/or advocating for UX consistency by creating flexible, reusable UI components.

Designers at Palantir develop a deep understanding of the problems our customers face while solving some of the world’s most unique challenges. Our mission is to build generalizable and scalable solutions that elegantly handle the complexity of these problem spaces.

Core Responsibilities
- Interaction and visual design . As a product designer, you'll be involved at every stage of design work. You'll help define early product concepts, flesh out the high-level workflow and micro-interactions of a feature, and execute on a crisp and effective visual design. You should have experience designing and prototyping using tools such as Figma.
- User research . We frequently do informal user research, and value people who can be flexible with research processes and methodologies to achieve the right outcome. You'll often visit customer offices to interview and learn from the users we serve. You'll pair qualitative methods (e.g. scripted usability tests and contextual inquiry) with quantitative information, like product and usage metrics.
- Deliver and communicate designs in close collaboration . We work closely with product and forward deployed engineers to realize our design ideas. You'll treat engineers and product managers as partners and collaborate with them to prototype and build out products.
- Awareness of how software interfaces are built. Familiarity with HTML, CSS, Javascript, and Typescript is appreciated. You don't need to be an expert—just fluent enough to collaborate with engineers, and know what's possible with frontend technologies.
- Designers at Palantir have great autonomy over their work, so a wide skill set is necessary. However, many designers on the team are also passionate experts in one area. You might be the kind of designer who ships code every week, or the kind of designer who shares detailed user research findings with your team.
What We Value
- Excellent collaboration and communication skills with the ability to build great relationships with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders, and convey and debate design rationale.
- High empathy and dedication to the user, striving to understand and empower them.
- An iterative design process. You validate your ideas early (with stakeholders and users) and are thoughtful and intentional in seeking and responding to feedback. You move fast, listen, and adapt. You rapidly incorporate feedback, and prioritize collaboration. You are adept at giving and receiving critiques.
- Excitement for solving hard, complex problems. You are excited to design for technically complex and data dense interfaces. You thrive in an environment where you can jump into deep subject matter expertise to define simple, approachable, yet still powerful product experiences.
- Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions when needed.
What We Require
- Must be planning on graduating in 2027.
- Active US Security clearance or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance.
- A portfolio demonstrating at least one software interface design project. If parts of your portfolio are password-protected, please include your portfolio password under 'Additional Questions' when applying.
Salary
 
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $125,000 - $130,000/year. title: Revenue Accounting Manager
text:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
The Finance Team supports and empowers Palantirians through both day-to-day operations and a solution-oriented approach to problem solving. As a member of the Revenue Team, you will be responsible for guiding your customer and deal portfolio through the quote-to-cash process, analysing and reviewing complex revenue transactions, as well as continually refining our revenue recognition policies. You will need to be able to articulate revenue guidance clearly while supporting the legal and deal team on contract drafting to maximise revenue. You will also provide direction on technical revenue accounting issues and be able to explain the accounting impact to the internal stakeholders across various teams including Business Development/Sales, Legal, and Finance during the contract negotiation process. You will work closely with Sales, Finance, and Accounts Receivable teams to ensure the health of your portfolio and participate in global month/quarter-end revenue close.
You are a hands-on self-starter who loves to collaborate, and who is always looking to improve upon the status quo. The position requires strong technical, analytical, attention to detail and communication skills.
 

Core Responsibilities
- Manage the revenue recognition process from the contract negotiation phase to financial statement disclosure.
- Partnering with Legal and Sales teams to optimise contractual structures to achieve business objectives while ensuring compliance with policies and revenue recognition rules.
- Exercise judgement while ensuring that accounting conclusions are documented in technical memos in accordance with policies and current software revenue recognition rules.
- Drive revenue and cost of revenue month-end close process by creating and validating accruals, preparing and reviewing journal entries and account reconciliations, ensuring policy compliance and developing standard reports.
- Provide technical guidance, training, and support to the Finance, Legal, and Business Development/Sales teams.
- Work actively with internal and external auditors to ensure that revenue recognition policies and interpretations are consistent and adhere to GAAP.
- Identify, champion, and implement continuous improvement initiatives related to revenue processes, including systems, reporting, and analysis.
- Partnering with business leadership and the Sales/Finance team on revenue forecasting processes.
What We Value
- Strong communications, presentation, and interpersonal skills, including the ability to summarise key accounting and operational issues to business partners and leadership.
- Complex analytical problem-solving and project management skills.
- Proficiency with NetSuite and/or other revenue recognition accounting systems.
- CPA or ACCA/ACA (preferred but not required).
What We Require
- Extensive experience in the application of ASC 606, specifically in its application to enterprise software-as-a-service.
- 5+ years’ experience within a large public accounting firm and/or a small to mid-sized enterprise software company.

Build software and deliver customer outcomes.  Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations around the world use data. Teams within Palantir’s Foundations organization are made up of a small number of engineers, each focused on one of four major categories of our infrastructure:
 
• Backend Infrastructure: Maximizes the productivity of our backend developers and ensures Palantir’s platforms have performant and consistent RESTful services. Think: making the “easy way” the “right way” when developing backend services, including designing infrastructure to build hundreds of micro-service repos performantly, or to ensure we keep reliable audit logs of everything users do in our platforms.
• Developer Infrastructure: Operates the systems and services that underpin all aspects of our developer ecosystem, including off-the-shelf tooling like GitHub and custom tooling for managing automated changes across hundreds of repositories.

• Storage Infrastructure: Develops Palantir’s database and search systems, which includes supporting storage technologies across cloud, on-premise, and classified or secure environments. title: Senior Data Scientist, Artist-First AI Music lab
text:
The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.
We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:
Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.
Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.
Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.
Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.
For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

What You'll Do
- Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music.
- Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms.
- Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction.
- Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations.
- Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust.
- Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify.
- Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact.
- Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly.
Who You Are 
- You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners.
- You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior.
- You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry.
- You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact.
- You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities.
- You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy.
- You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis.
- You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces.
Where You'll Be 
- We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home
- This team operates within the US Eastern timezone for collaboration
The United States base range for this position is $144,714–$206,735 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future.

title: Legal Counsel, Litigation and Copyright
text:
Spotify's Legal team is growing. We're facing innovative challenges that mirror the groundbreaking industry and product at the heart of our company. As we've expanded into more than 180 markets and our business has grown tremendously, we find ourselves facing new and interesting legal issues every day — including an increasing volume of patent disputes alongside the copyright and content matters that have always been central to our work.
As Legal Counsel, Litigation, you will work on a variety of litigation, copyright, patent, and other contentious and advisory matters, and help craft the way our company thinks about and handles them. The work we face is constantly developing, and the workload is growing faster than we can, so we will look to you to think thoughtfully about processes and policies that will help meet our goals. What You'll Do

- Stay current on developments in patent and copyright law, particularly as they affect the technology and media industries.
Who You Are
- You hold a law degree (or equivalent) from a top-flight law school and are qualified to practice law as in-house counsel in the State of New York.

- You have experience with e-discovery and managing complex, multi-jurisdictional disputes.
- You have experience contributing to teams that drive successful outcomes on complex matters.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, HPC
text:
Zoox is looking for an experienced Senior/Staff Software Engineer to build, scale, and operate our custom High-Performance Computing infrastructure. As Zoox scales its autonomous vehicle development, our HPC platform must keep pace with rapidly growing compute, storage, and scheduling demands across the company. You will modernize our HPC platform—built on industry-leading technologies like Ray.io, SLURM, and Kubernetes—with a focus on reliability, scalability, and world-class developer velocity.
 
These HPC services form the backbone of development workflows across all Zoox software teams, from data engineering to training our AI models in Perception, Planner, Prediction, to Simulation, and more. You will have a direct impact on the productivity and effectiveness of every engineering team at Zoox.
 
The position comes with a high degree of independence and the opportunity to define Zoox's HPC platform strategy, both technically and organizationally. You will work closely with stakeholders in Autonomy and Software teams to understand their workload requirements and translate them into robust, scalable infrastructure.

In this role, you will:
- 
 Design and implement core services and abstractions for distributed compute infrastructure supporting hundreds of thousands of concurrent jobs
- 
 Work with customer teams and other infrastructure teams to build a multiyear software engineering roadmap for the HPC platform
- 
 Lead multi-quarter, cross team initiatives that drive org-wide improvements
- 
 Create production-grade APIs, SDKs, and tools that make it easy for engineers across Zoox to run large-scale distributed workloads
- 
 Design and improve job scheduling algorithms and auto-scaling policies to maximize reliability and resource availability
- 
 Design multi-region orchestration strategies that optimize for data locality, reliability, and performance
- 
 Identify and resolve systemic reliability and performance issues through profiling, analysis, and collaboration with workload owners across multiple teams
- 
 Evaluate new technologies and paradigms that improve Zoox's computational and storage capabilities
- 
 Develop capacity planning tools and forecasting models to support Zoox's growing compute needs
- 
 Mentor junior engineers, guiding them through their career development
Qualifications
- 
 Experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems in production
- 
 Experience with Ray.io, particularly Ray Core and Ray Data (or equivalent technologies)
- 
 Experience with Kubernetes, particularly for heterogeneous workloads
- 
 Experience with cloud infrastructure on AWS or similar providers
- 
 Track record of shipping and operating reliable, highly available scalable infrastructure
- 
 Demonstrated ability to prioritize development work and build cross-functional consensus around technical tradeoffs
- 
 Proficiency with Python
Bonus Qualifications
- 
 Exposure to machine learning workloads (training, inference, data generation)
- 
 Experience with Kubernetes or SLURM at scale (>10k+ nodes)
- 
 Experience with SLURM workload manager and advanced scheduling policies
- 
 Background in algorithmic optimization or operations research
- 
 Experience building developer tools and platforms used by large engineering organizations
About Zoox
 
Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

title: Senior Supplier Quality Engineer
text:
The Senior Supplier Quality Engineer will play a key role in ensuring world-class performance of the Zoox prototype and production Seating and Vehicle Interiors supply base, and drive continuous improvement. The ideal candidate will be entrepreneurial, driven, energetic, detailed, and team-oriented, with deep hands-on knowledge of seat systems and interior trim manufacturing.
Candidates with experience across seating and interior commodities — seat structures and mechanisms, foam-in-place and molded foam, cut-and-sew and trim covers, door trim, headliners, and carpet — and a strong working understanding of manufacturing processes such as injection molding, foam molding, cut-and-sew, lamination and wrapping, welding and stamping of seat frames, and electromechanical sub-assembly will be highly preferred.

In this role, you will: 
- Partner with Vehicle Interiors Engineering, Design, and Strategic Sourcing to select suppliers based on manufacturing capability, capacity, and quality maturity.
- Collaborate with suppliers on design reviews to ensure seats and interior trim parts are manufacturable, and explore new production techniques and materials where needed.
-  Lead the supplier industrialization process from design through production ramp-up, including soft tooling to hard tooling transitions.
- Support suppliers with tooling, foam molds, sew fixtures, gauges, and process qualifications; witness and approve tooling and process buy-offs on site.
- Drive the APQP process and support PPAP through start of production, including dimensional, material, appearance, and performance validation.
- Own craftsmanship and appearance quality for occupant-facing surfaces — grain, gloss, color and material matching, gap and flush, seam quality, stitch integrity, and trim fit — and establish master and boundary sample processes with suppliers.
-  Ensure supplier compliance with seating safety and interior material requirements, including occupant safety performance, flammability, and durability testing.
-  Assess supplier readiness for vehicle builds and help manage production risk ahead of each build phase.
- Train suppliers on Zoox quality systems and review prototype and production part quality documentation.
- Lead root cause and corrective action efforts (8D) for supplier quality issues, and support Manufacturing, Quality, and Vehicle Engineering with analysis and disposition of suspect supplier material.
- Monitor and report supplier quality metrics to drive ongoing improvement across the seating and interiors supply base.
-  Use lean and quality tools to improve yield, first-time-through quality, and cycle time throughout the supply base.
- Improve Zoox supplier quality processes such as supplier assessments, supplier management, part approval, and corrective actions.
- Be ready for up to 40% domestic and international travel, sometimes on short notice.
Qualifications 
- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Materials, or a related engineering field.
- 8+ years of experience in quality, supplier quality, or manufacturing — ideally in automotive. 
- Direct experience with seating and/or interior trim commodities and their supply base.
- Hands-on experience launching new products (NPI) and creating or improving quality systems.
- Experience with manufacturing processes such as injection molding, foam-in-place and molded foam, cut-and-sew, lamination and wrapping, stamping and welding, and electromechanical assembly.
- Skilled in structured problem-solving methods such as Six Sigma, 8D, Pareto analysis, DOE, fishbone, and Is/Is-Not.
- Familiar with core quality tools: process flow diagrams, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, and process capability studies.
Bonus Qualifications 
- Experience with seat safety and regulatory requirements, and with seat and trim durability and abuse testing.
- Experience with soft trim materials — leather, textiles, TPO/PVC skins, foams and adhesives — and with material and appearance approval processes.
- Experience with seat comfort and craftsmanship evaluation, including CMF (color, material, finish) alignment with Design.
- Familiarity with seat electronics and mechanisms such as occupant detection sensors, heaters, motors, recliners, and tracks.
-  Experience with tooling and fixture validation.
- Certifications such as CQE, ASQ Quality Auditor, or Six Sigma Green/Black Belt.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Perception
text:
As a Perception Engineer, you will be instrumental in designing and implementing cutting-edge detection models, utilizing fused sensor data. In particular, the role will be on advanced projects that are aimed at the next generation of driving software, including looking at joint detection and tracking models as well as ways to send rich embeddings to downstream models to relay semantic meaning and capture uncertainty. 
 
This role offers a unique opportunity to directly impact Zoox's expansion into new areas. By developing more generalizable and adaptable models, you will help us navigate diverse and challenging circumstances, accelerating our mission to deliver safe and reliable autonomous mobility. We are looking for a highly motivated individual passionate about pushing the boundaries of perception in the autonomous vehicle space.

In this role, you will:
- Train ML models, perform various studies into incorporating SOTA approaches as well as ablations/modifications of existing models
- Document experimental outcomes and drive towards deploying these models into Zoox robots
- Visualize your data at the input and output to understand the issues
- Collaborate with teams such as ML optimization, data labeling, metrics and planner to ensure project is successful for Zoox releases
Qualifications
- MS/PhD in Computer Science or related field
- Experience with PyTorch or related ML frameworks
- Experience deploying learned models into production
- Excellent collaboration and teamwork skills with proven track record of working on large-scale problems
Bonus Qualifications
- Prior experience in the AV or related space with joint detection and tracking models
- Deep understanding of how to setup end-to-end training and evaluation processes
About Zoox
Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

Follow us on LinkedIn

Accommodations
If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process please reach out to accommodations@zoox.com or your assigned recruiter.

A Final Note:
You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Zoox, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.

title: Manager, Technical Program Management (Advanced Hardware Manufacturing)
text:
As Manager, Technical Program Management, you will lead the team responsible for coordinating prototype sensor and compute hardware programs and supporting their transition to high-volume serial manufacturing. You will partner with leaders across hardware, software, vehicle engineering, product, manufacturing, and finance to turn strategic priorities into executable plans. Your team will maintain schedules, define milestones, track resources and budgets, identify risks, and communicate progress to stakeholders.

In this job, you will
- 
 Partner with department leaders to translate company priorities and milestones into product roadmaps, program schedules, and defined deliverables.
- 
 Oversee technical programs for high-volume serial manufacturing, including production readiness, capacity planning, ramp milestones, and the resolution of issues that affect output.
- 
 Coordinate the transition from prototype builds to serial production with engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and contract manufacturing partners.
- 
 Work with functional leaders and finance to plan and track headcount, budgets, and other program resources. Establish clear ownership, dependencies, and delivery expectations across participating teams.
- 
 Define and maintain program management processes, operating rhythms, and decision forums.
- 
 Identify risks early, make their impact visible, and coordinate mitigation plans with engineering and manufacturing teams.
- 
 Prepare decision points for leadership meetings, including the information and recommendations needed to resolve blockers.
Qualifications
- 
 Bachelor’s or master’s degree in an engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- 
 12+ years of experience in engineering, technical program management, or management consulting.
- 
 5+ years of experience managing Technical Program Managers.
- 
 Experience with hardware development, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
- 
 Experience working with contract manufacturers.
Bonus Qualifications
- 
 Demonstrated success leading complex programs involving multiple functions.
- 
 Experience supporting high-volume serial manufacturing.
- 
 Ability to build effective working relationships with senior leaders and engineers across disciplines.
- 
 Experience handling confidential business and technical information with discretion.

title: Shift / Team Lead, Readiness & Response (2nd Shift)
text:
As a Team Lead for Readiness and Response within Zoox’s Fleet Operations organization, you are at the forefront of the autonomous mobility revolution. You will be a key leader in our expansion into new markets, responsible for the end-to-end operational integrity of the Zoox Robotaxi and Mapping Vehicle Fleet. This role unifies the technical preparation of our vehicles (Readiness) with high-level oversight of live field incidents (Response), ensuring every Zoox vehicle is "service ready" and every mission is supported with operational excellence.

Your leadership will bridge the gap between structured depot workflows and the dynamic environment of real-time fleet response. Rather than performing hands-on technical tasks, you will drive strategy and performance by managing a hybrid workforce of Full-Time Shift Leads and contingent associates. Serving as the primary on-site escalation path for critical field incidents and holding third-party recovery partners accountable, you will directly impact Zoox’s fleet availability, safety standards, and our ability to deliver a seamless experience to our riders.
 
Travel Requirements: less than 20%
 
Shift: 2nd Shift, Tuesday - Saturday, 4pm - 12am

In this role, you will:
- Collaborate with Leadership: Work with Fleet Ops leaders in market, as well as Fleet Ops Program Teams, to ensure optimization of fleet utilization while driving market needs.
- Drive Unified Fleet Strategy: Oversee the execution of operational strategies for both vehicle preparation (Readiness) and incident response (Response), ensuring alignment with broader organizational uptime goals.
- Lead through Shift Leadership: Directly manage and mentor FTE Shift Leads & a contingent workforce, empowering them to oversee daily floor operations while you focus on high-level strategy, performance coaching, and site-wide operational health.
- Manage On-Site Escalations: Serve as the primary leadership escalation path for critical field incidents and service interferences, providing guidance to the team and making high-level decisions to resolve complex vehicle or rider issues.
- Manage a Hybrid Workforce: Provide administrative and people leadership for a multidisciplinary team, including onboarding, training, and performance management for contingent (contract) workforces.
- Coordinate Third-Party Vendors On The Ground: Serve as the local point of contact for vehicle recovery, roadside assistance, and facility vendors — verifying on-site service quality and response time, and flagging no-shows, defects, or service misses to the relevant Program team, who owns vendor standards, governance, and corrective action.
- Optimize Operational Workflows: Identify bottlenecks in depot workflows (software deployment, sensor cleaning), field response protocols, and work with cross-functional partners to implement process innovations to reduce vehicle downtime.
- Ensure Regulatory & Safety Compliance: Oversee adherence to all health and safety policies (OSHA) within the workshop and ensure all vehicle documentation and "Up/Down" status reporting are accurate and audit-ready.
- Synthesize Operational Data: Own the analysis and reporting of site-specific KPIs, providing leadership with data-driven insights into fleet health, team efficiency, and vendor performance.
Qualifications
- 8+ years of relevant work experience in an operations-based environment
- Experience Managing People Leaders: Demonstrated ability to manage and develop direct reports at the Shift Lead or Supervisor level.
- Contingent Workforce Management: Extensive experience leading, onboarding, and managing the performance of contractor or contingent workforces.
- Vendor & Partner Management: Demonstrated experience managing 3rd party service providers and holding external partners accountable to Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
- Critical Thinking under Pressure: Ability to manage high-priority escalations and make sound, data-driven decisions in fast-paced or ambiguous situations.
- Technical Aptitude: Ability to understand complex technical systems (autonomous vehicle hardware/software) to effectively lead technical teams and communicate with engineering stakeholders.
- Process Improvement Mindset: Experience facilitating Lean Six Sigma projects or similar methodologies to improve operational efficiency.
- Safety Excellence: Commitment to maintaining a culture of safety and compliance; must have a clean driving record.
Bonus Qualifications
- Bachelor's Degree in a relevant field (business management, operations, finance, etc.)
- Experience with autonomous vehicles, or a similar safety-critical industry
- Experience in a fast-paced and dynamic service environment.
- Experience with Lean Six Sigma or other process optimization methodologies.
- Familiarity with fleet management software.

title: Senior / Staff Technical Program Manager, Fleet Optimization
text:
Zoox's Fleet Operations Program Management team delivers cross-functional programs critical to the growth, expansion, and efficient operation of our commercial autonomous vehicle service. We partner closely with Fleet Operations and cross-functional stakeholders to verify, validate, and launch new software on our fleet — while continuously maturing our operational processes to deliver a premium customer experience.
 
We're looking for an experienced, forward-thinking Senior / Staff Program Manager to help define and execute strategies that scale our Verification & Validation (V&V) operations. Our testing fleet — hundreds of vehicles across multiple cities and private tracks — is growing rapidly in size and geographic reach. This is a highly cross-functional role operating at the intersection of operations, autonomy, engineering, and product — requiring someone who can navigate technical complexity while driving alignment and execution across a broad set of stakeholders.
 

Expected Travel: 10–15%

In this role, you will:
- Lead and coordinate large-scale, highly cross-functional programs spanning Autonomy, Product, Infrastructure, Engineering, and Safety teams to drive measurable improvements in fleet efficiency and software quality
- Own and drive operational efficiency initiatives that span multiple engineering, field service, and operations teams — identifying bottlenecks, aligning stakeholders, and unblocking downstream execution
- Partner with System Design & Mission Assurance and other safety teams to gather and pressure-test requirements — bringing a critical lens to ensure what's being asked for is the right thing to build or prioritize
- Champion the adoption of AI and data-driven tools within operations — including building centralized, multi-source reporting systems that surface actionable intelligence from the field and feed into leadership decision-making
- Run monthly business reviews (MBRs) with a broad set of stakeholders — synthesizing ground-level signals from market leads and operational locations into clear recommendations on resources, partnerships, and priorities for leadership
- Define and track the right operational metrics — not just reporting on what exists, but actively shaping what should be measured and why
- Partner with Finance to support operational and financial planning cycles (OP1, OP2, quarterly R&O), ensuring budgets reflect operational needs accurately and efficiently
- Lead key efficiency initiatives across our L3 and robotaxi R&D fleets, including improvements in fleet utilization, time-in-autonomy, troubleshooting cycle times, and operational infrastructure
- Manage program timelines, resources, and deliverables; proactively identify and mitigate operational and programmatic risks
- Create and maintain program documentation and progress reports for senior leadership
Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Research, Operations Management, or a STEM field
- 10+ years of program management experience, with a strong preference for backgrounds that blend technical depth with operational execution
- Demonstrated ability to lead large-scale, highly cross-functional programs with significant organizational impact
- Comfortable operating in ambiguity — able to structure undefined problems, build frameworks from scratch, and drive toward clarity
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills across engineering, product, and operations audiences
- Deeply data-driven — not just tracking metrics but validating them, questioning outputs that don't add up, and pushing back when the data tells the wrong story
- Proficient with modern AI tools and workflows (e.g., Gemini, Claude, MCP APIs, cloud-based coding environments) and actively applies them to drive operational efficiency and better decision-making
Bonus Qualifications
- Experience in autonomous vehicles, aerospace, ride-hail, robotics, or fleet management
- Background in systems engineering, software development, or technical operations
- MBA or Master's degree in a STEM field
- PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification
- Experience with vehicle testing, validation, or disengagement analysis
