title: Deputy Program Manager, Test Range
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB OVERVIEW

The Test Range Coordinator is Saronic’s primary interface to U.S. Government test ranges for live-fire, missile, and target test events conducted aboard our autonomous surface vessels. You will own the end-to-end coordination of each range event — from initial scheduling and safety approvals, through launcher installation and checkout, vessel movement to the range, ordnance onload, and live test execution, to post-event launcher de-installation and demobilization. Acting as the connective tissue between Saronic engineering and operations, the Government customer, payload and effector providers, and the range authorities, you will make sure every stakeholder has the access, documentation, and information needed to execute a safe, on-schedule, and successful test.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Range scheduling & access

 - Serve as Saronic’s single point of contact to U.S. Government test ranges — including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station / Space Launch Delta 45 (Eastern Range), the Point Mugu Sea Range (NAWCWD, Naval Base Ventura County), and the Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF) — as well as other Major Range and Test Facility Base (MRTFB) sites as programs require.

 - Submit, track, and maintain range-use requests and Universal Documentation System (UDS) products (e.g., Program Introduction, Program Requirements, and Operations Requirements documents), and negotiate and lock test windows on range schedules.

 - Coordinate range instrumentation, tracking, optics, telemetry, and Time-Space-Position Information (TSPI) requirements, along with frequency/spectrum requests, with range personnel.

 - Manage schedule conflicts, slip planning, and re-baselining across multiple concurrent test campaigns.

Safety, ordnance & regulatory approvals

 - Develop and shepherd range safety packages, hazard analyses, mission rules, and launch commit criteria through range safety and flight safety boards.

 - Coordinate ordnance transportation, explosives safety siting, and Explosives Safety Quantity-Distance (ESQD) requirements in accordance with DoD and range explosives safety standards.

 - Coordinate ordnance/effector onload, staging, arming and de-arming, and disposition, including Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) and range safety support.

 - Support environmental and regulatory compliance, including Notices to Mariners and Airmen (NOTMAR/NOTAM) and marine-mammal and environmental monitoring requirements.

Test event planning & execution

 - Build and maintain the integrated schedule for each test event, spanning launcher hardware installation, checkout, vessel movement to the range, ordnance onload, execution, and de-installation.

 - Coordinate logistics for vessel transport to and from the range (over-the-road and/or marine transit), launch and recovery, and support and safety craft.

 - Lead Test Readiness Reviews (TRRs), rehearsals and dry runs, and go/no-go processes, and run day-of coordination among range control, the Saronic test team, and payload providers.

 - Manage post-test launcher de-installation, demobilization, range clearance, and event close-out, including data hand-off and lessons learned.

Stakeholder & information management

 - Act as the information hub across Saronic, the Government customer, and payload/effector providers, maintaining shared schedules, action-item logs, interface documentation, and status reporting.

 - Coordinate the flow of technical and programmatic information, including handling of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and classified material in accordance with program security requirements.

 - Facilitate interface control between Saronic vessel and launcher hardware and third-party effectors, missiles, and targets (e.g., aerial and surface target drones).

 - Support the agreements and funding mechanisms that enable range use




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, a physical science, logistics/operations management, or a related field — or equivalent military/operational experience in lieu of a degree.

 - 3–6 years of experience in test range operations, missile/weapons or flight test, range safety, or military test and operations.

 - Working knowledge of U.S. Government test range scheduling, safety, and documentation processes.

 - Familiarity with ordnance and explosives handling and safety requirements.

 - Demonstrated ability to plan and coordinate complex, multi-stakeholder events against a fixed schedule and budget.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to brief both technical teams and Government leadership.

 - Willingness and ability to travel frequently (up to ~50–75% during active test periods) and to work on the waterfront and aboard vessels in an outdoor marine environment.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 - Prior working relationships with, or direct experience at, the Point Mugu Sea Range / NAWCWD, PMRF, Cape Canaveral / SLD 45, Eglin / Gulf Range, White Sands Missile Range, or similar ranges.

 - Military background in surface warfare, aviation ordnance, gunner’s mate, EOD, range operations, or space/missile operations (U.S. Navy, USSF, USMC, Army, or USAF).

 - Experience with unmanned/autonomous surface vessels (USV/ASV) or other maritime platforms. 

 - Familiarity with missile/effector integration, launchers, and fire-control interfaces.

 - Knowledge of the Universal Documentation System (UDS) and Major Range and Test Facility Base (MRTFB) processes.

 - Familiarity with DoD explosives safety standards (e.g., DoD 6055.09-M) and range safety documentation.

 - Active Secret clearance (or higher).

 - Project management certification (e.g., PMP) or equivalent demonstrated experience.

 - Small-boat operations experience or relevant U.S. Coast Guard credentials.


TRAVEL & WORK ENVIRONMENTS 

 - Significant travel to test ranges, with extended on-site stays around test windows; travel is campaign-driven and may exceed 50% during active test periods.

 - Work is performed at Saronic facilities, on the waterfront, and aboard vessels — including outdoors, in marine conditions, and around heavy equipment and ordnance.

 - Must be able to work non-standard hours, including early mornings, nights, and weekends, to meet range windows and weather/sea-state constraints.

 - Must be able to lift and carry equipment, board vessels, and wear required personal protective equipment (PPE); reasonable accommodations will be considered.

title: Design Manager
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

A mid-level professional who independently leads design teams on small to mid sized infrastructure project design and construction scopes, translating requirements into high-quality deliverables with minimal oversight. Participates in design critiques, iterates on feedback effectively, and contributes meaningfully to team design discussions. Preferably professionally licensed/PMP or on track to become licensed in their area of practice. title: Shipyard Technical Manager
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



As the Shipyard Technical Manager at Saronic-Franklin, you will lead the technical execution and operational integration of Production and Engineering activities across the shipyard. This role is responsible for ensuring vessel construction activities are technically sound, production-ready, efficiently executed, and aligned with quality, schedule, and safety objectives.

The Shipyard Technical Manager will oversee the production engineering team, which supports scheduling, planning, production flow analysis and improvement, industrial engineering activities, and provides expertise across all labor trades in the shipyard. The Shipyard Technical Manager will also oversee the Manufacturing Engineering team, which supports workstation tooling, processes, and improvements, operates the machine shop, and recommends product design improvements. Finally, the Shipyard Technical Manager will work directly with the Design Engineering and Build Engineering leadership to ensure cross-functional agreement on product design improvements. This position plays a critical role in enabling scalable and repeatable vessel construction operations within a fast-paced maritime manufacturing environment.


KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

1. Team Leadership: Manage, train, and motivate a team of production and manufacturing engineering personnel, including hiring, performance evaluations, and professional development.

2. Engineering Oversight: Ensure production and manufacturing engineering deliverables support efficient vessel construction, including work packages, installation planning, technical issue resolution, and production readiness.

3. Production and Manufacturing Engineering Management: Identify and implement continuous improvement initiatives related to production flow, scheduling, planning, build sequencing, and technical operations performance. Develop and optimize manufacturing processes, tooling strategies, workflow layouts, and resource utilization to improve workstation efficiency, reduce waste, and support scalable shipyard operations.

4. Build Engineering Coordination: Coordinate with build engineering leadership to ensure effective execution of activities related to structural assembly, vessel systems integration, outfitting coordination, and product design improvements to ensure technical alignment across departments.

5. Quality Assurance: Ensure engineering and manufacturing activities comply with company standards, shipyard procedures, regulatory requirements, and applicable maritime industry specifications.

6. 8. Safety Compliance: Work with the EHS team to enforce workplace safety protocols and ensure engineering-driven production activities are executed in accordance with Saronic EHS guidelines and company policies.

7. Reporting and Operational Metrics: Monitor and report key performance indicators (KPIs) related to production efficiency, engineering throughput, build execution, schedule performance, labor utilization, downtime for repair (DFR), and technical issue resolution.

Shipyard Technical Managers at Saronic-Franklin are expected to have the knowledge, skill, and ability to accomplish the below:


TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE

1. Strong understanding of shipyard production operations, vessel construction sequencing, manufacturing processes, and marine production systems.

2. Ability to lead cross-functional engineering and production teams in a fast-paced shipbuilding environment.

3. Experience interpreting engineering drawings, production work packages, technical specifications, and vessel integration requirements.

4. Ability to analyze and make key operational decisions related to production workflows, staffing, manufacturing methods, tooling, and engineering priorities.

5. Ability to communicate effectively with executive leadership, engineering teams, production personnel, suppliers, and shipyard stakeholders.

6. Strong technical aptitude, organizational skills, and attention to detail.

7. Maintain proper administrative records, technical documentation, and operational reporting.


JOB PROFICIENCY

1. Ensure Production Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering teams are accomplishing tasks, roles, and responsibilities as outlined in applicable job descriptions and operational objectives.

2. Provide independent judgement to leadership regarding team performance, staffing needs, organizational structure, and operational improvements using established policies, procedures, and practices.

3. Resolve and document technical production issues impacting vessel construction, manufacturing operations, quality, or schedule performance.

4. Manage overall technical resource utilization to meet or exceed production and operational efficiency goals.

5. Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on manufacturing efficiency, production scalability, technical execution, and operational excellence.

6. Provide periodic operational documentation, technical status updates, engineering issue reporting, and shift turnover communication for compliance and continuous improvement purposes.

7. Collaborate with product design team, project management team, and build engineering team to ensure product design is in line with scaled production goals. This includes participating in conflict resolution re: design vs production issues

1. Facilitating as-built updates to drawings

2. Deriving, tracking, and implementing lessons learned in design-for-production

3. Facilitating design-for-production improvements


CULTURE AND COLLABORATION

1. Follow all shipyard safety policies, including proper use of PPE, fire prevention, and confined space protocols.

2. Assist in the training and development of all engineers and engineering management on site.

3. Collaborate and communicate effectively with all shipyard departments to ensure seamless vessel production integration.

4. Work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced maritime manufacturing environment.

5. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.

6. Maintain a positive attitude toward customers and represent Saronic professionally.

7. Make a personal commitment and be accountable for EHS results, driving toward the achievement of defined operational goals.

8. Maintain a supportive and productive work atmosphere through professional conduct and effective communication with internal and external customers, including vendors, coworkers, subordinates, and leadership teams.

9. Promote a culture of technical excellence, operational discipline, accountability, and continuous improvement throughout the shipyard organization.


QUALIFICATIONS

Required

· 10+ years of shipbuilding, heavy manufacturing, or maritime industrial experience

· Experience leading vessel construction, production operations, or manufacturing engineering teams

· Strong understanding of modular construction, production sequencing, and waterfront operations

· Experience managing cross-functional teams including production, engineering, planning, and quality

· Demonstrated success improving production efficiency, throughput, quality, and schedule performance

Preferred

· Experience in advanced manufacturing, industrialization, automation, or digital production systems

title: Electrical Engineer – UUVs & Undersea Electronics
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB OVERVIEW

We are seeking a Senior Electrical Engineer to lead the design, development, integration, and testing of advanced electrical and electronic systems for unmanned underwater vehicles, undersea sensors, and subsea mission systems. This role is ideal for an experienced engineer with strong expertise in embedded electronics, power systems, sensor integration, communications, and ruggedized hardware designed for harsh marine environments.

The Senior Electrical Engineer will work closely with mechanical, software, systems, autonomy, and test engineering teams to deliver reliable undersea platforms and payloads capable of operating in demanding subsea conditions. The role requires a hands-on technical leader who can move between architecture, detailed design, troubleshooting, vendor coordination, and field testing.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Electrical System Design
   
   - Design and develop electrical architectures for UUVs, AUVs, ROVs, subsea payloads, and related support equipment.
   
   - Develop power distribution systems, battery interfaces, motor control electronics, embedded control boards, sensor interfaces, communication buses, and data acquisition systems.
   
   - Create schematics, PCB layouts, cable drawings, wiring diagrams, interface control documents, and electrical design documentation.
   
   - Select components for subsea and high-reliability applications, including connectors, penetrators, batteries, sensors, embedded processors, power converters, and communication modules.

 - Undersea Electronics & Integration
   
   - Integrate electronics into pressure housings, subsea enclosures, wet-mate interfaces, and vehicle hull structures.
   
   - Support design considerations related to pressure, corrosion, galvanic isolation, thermal management, sealing, shock, vibration, and long-duration underwater operation.
   
   - Develop and troubleshoot interfaces for sonar, acoustic modems, inertial navigation systems, depth sensors, Doppler velocity logs, cameras, payload sensors, thrusters, and mission computers.
   
   - Support electrical integration of autonomous vehicle subsystems, including propulsion, navigation, control, communications, payloads, and energy storage.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

 - Typically 7+ years of electrical engineering experience, with significant experience developing embedded, ruggedized, or mission-critical electronics.

 - Experience designing, integrating, and troubleshooting electrical systems for UUVs, AUVs, ROVs, subsea systems, marine robotics, defense systems, aerospace systems, or other harsh-environment platforms.

 - Strong knowledge of analog and digital circuit design, power electronics, embedded systems, communication interfaces, and sensor integration.

 - Familiarity with electrical interfaces such as Ethernet, RS-232, RS-485, CAN, SPI, I2C, USB, serial communications, and timing/synchronization signals.

 - Experience with battery-powered systems, power budgeting, DC power distribution, grounding, isolation, EMI/EMC mitigation, and fault protection.

 - Hands-on experience building, testing, debugging, and modifying prototype hardware.

 - Ability to create clear engineering documentation, test procedures, interface control documents, and technical reports.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced engineering environment with multidisciplinary teams.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Ocean Engineering, Robotics, or a related field.

 - Experience with subsea electrical connectors, pressure-rated housings, cable assemblies, penetrators, oil-filled systems, or wet-mateable interfaces.

 - Experience with undersea navigation, acoustic communications, sonar systems, payload electronics, or vehicle control systems.

 - Knowledge of UUV mission architectures, autonomy systems, subsea sensing, or maritime defense applications.

title: Mission Operations Specialist (Product)
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



The Mission Operations Specialist sits at the point where our vessels meet the customer. You plan and run ASV missions, provide on-site technical support to DoD partners during integration and operations, and coordinate the projects and programs that carry that work from concept to delivery.

This role requires frequent travel to partner and customer locations, domestically and internationally, up to 50% of the time.

You will work closely with team members, stakeholders, and other departments to ensure successful delivery of assigned project and program objectives.

Projects are defined as work that ends with the delivery of an expected outcome or end date. E.g. payload integration and demonstration of function.

Programs are defined as longer, less terminal workstreams such as ongoing product improvement and development roadmaps. E.g. supporting the ongoing development and testing of a vessel such as Corsair.

 

Responsibilities

 - On-Site Technical Support: Provide on-site technical support and assistance to partners and customers during product integration, installation, commissioning, and ongoing operations. Troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues related to our autonomous surface vessels, systems, and software

 - System Integration: Collaborate with partners and customers to integrate our autonomous surface vessels into their existing systems and infrastructure. Ensure seamless interoperability and compatibility between our products and their operational environment. Support system-level testing and validation activities

 - Customer Training and Documentation: Conduct training sessions and workshops to educate partners and customers on the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of our products. Develop training materials, user guides, and technical documentation to facilitate knowledge transfer and best practices

 - Remote Support and Troubleshooting: Provide remote technical support to partners and customers, leveraging communication tools and remote access capabilities. Diagnose and troubleshoot issues, guide users through problem resolution, and escalate complex issues to the appropriate teams for further investigation

 - Field Testing and Validation: Participate in field testing and validation activities at partner and customer locations. Collect data, assess performance, and provide feedback to the engineering and design teams. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to address any identified issues and implement necessary improvements

 - Customer Relationship Management: Build strong relationships with partners and customers by delivering exceptional technical support and fostering effective communication. Understand their needs, gather feedback, and advocate for their requirements internally. Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to define goals, objectives, and deliverables. Act as a technical liaison between partners/customers and Saronic internal teams

 - Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities for process improvements and product enhancements based on customer feedback and on-site experiences. Collaborate with internal teams to implement changes and contribute to the ongoing improvement of our products and services

 - Travel Management: Coordinate travel logistics and scheduling for on-site visits. Ensure timely and efficient travel arrangements, including transportation, accommodation, and necessary equipment

 - Planning: Work between internal and external stakeholders such as DoD customers, facilitating communication, managing expectations, and ensuring mission or program requirements are met. You will support the team through development of comprehensive mission plans, considering factors such as route optimization, environmental conditions, and risk mitigation to achieve desired outcomes.

 - ASV Operations and Monitoring: Operate ASV operations during missions, monitoring vessel performance, sensor data, and mission progress in real time. Troubleshoot technical issues and implement contingency plans to ensure mission continuity. Maintain situational awareness of maritime environments and adjust mission parameters as needed

 - Data Analysis and Reporting: Collect, analyze, and interpret data acquired during ASV missions to derive actionable insights. Generate comprehensive mission reports detailing key findings, observations, and recommendations. Provide feedback to the engineering and development teams for continuous improvement of ASV capabilities.

 - Compliance and Safety: Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, DoD policies, and industry standards related to ASV operations. Implement safety protocols and procedures to mitigate operational risks and ensure personnel safety.

Role Requirements

 - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Advanced degree preferred

 - Minimum of 3 years of experience in a field support or customer-facing technical role, preferably with complex hardware or software systems

 - Demonstrated success in project coordination and leadership in current role.

 - Valid driver's license and willingness to operate company vehicles or rental cars as needed

 - Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with team members, stakeholders, and senior management.

 - Strong leadership qualities, including the ability to motivate and inspire team members.

 - Job requires up to 50% travel.

 - Able to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water, lift up to 75 lbs., and spend extended time periods on the water.

Qualifications

 - Prior SOF and Military experience working with the DoD or other government agencies is a plus or equivalent experience

 - Experience in maritime operations, particularly with autonomous or unmanned systems is a plus

 - Proficiency in mission planning software, GIS tools, and maritime navigation systems

 - Strong technical knowledge of autonomous systems, robotics, or marine vessels, including their integration, operation, and troubleshooting

 - Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with a track record of diagnosing and resolving complex technical issues in real-world environments

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - Customer-oriented mindset with a passion for delivering exceptional support and building long-term relationships with partners and customers

Physical Demands

title: Supply Chain Planner
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB OVERVIEW

We are looking for a Supply Chain Planner II to manage and optimize the flow of materials,
components, and information for our autonomous surface vessels. This individual will play a critical role in forecasting demand, managing inventory levels, and supporting production, NPI, and/or non-steady state operations. You will partner closely with engineering, procurement, program management, and suppliers to ensure material readiness while balancing cost, risk, and schedule in dynamic environments. As a key member of our team, you will be responsible for maintaining our
supply chain's integrity, meeting deadlines, and ensuring compliance with DoD regulations and standards.




RESPONSIBILITIES 

 - Own and improve end-to-end tactical supply plans to support NPI builds, production builds, and/or off-nominal builds.

 - Translate engineering demand, build schedules, and program milestones into executable material requirements within ERP/MRP systems, ensuring system-driven visibility and control.

 - Optimize factory planning parameters (lead times, lot sizes, safety stock, planning fences, reorder strategies) to improve material flow, reduce shortages, and support rapid design iteration.

 - Drive BOM maturity and change management execution by assessing material impact of ECOs, managing cut-ins/cut-outs, and minimizing excess and obsolete exposure.

 - Identify and mitigate material readiness risks related to design instability, supplier capacity constraints, long-lead components, and quality performance through structured risk registers and recovery plans.

   parameters) to enable reliable MRP outputs and production readiness signals.

 - Establish and monitor material readiness metrics (shortage tracking, kit completeness, on-time-to-build, supplier OTD, inventory health) to drive daily execution and escalation.

 - Lead shortage resolution and recovery management, including root cause analysis, systemic corrective actions, and supplier coordination to protect build schedules.

 - Develop and implement supply planning processes, workflows, and system utilization to improve repeatability, scalability, and factory throughput.

 - Analyze supply chain performance data to identify systemic bottlenecks and implement
   process improvements that balance speed, cost, inventory exposure, and risk.

 - Ensure compliance with DoD program requirements, audit readiness, and traceability standards through disciplined documentation and system controls

title: Mechanic (Deployable)
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB SUMMARY



Saronic is seeking a Mechanic IV to serve as the senior hands-on technician for our deployable maintenance footprint, supporting our autonomous platforms, including the 12 ft UUV, the 24 ft Corsair, and the 52 ft Mirage, at test sites, depots, and forward operating locations. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Deployable Operations within the Sustainment organization, you will diagnose, repair, and sustain diesel, mechanical, electrical, and integrated vehicle systems in the field and set the technical and quality standard the rest of the team works to.

This is the most senior wrench on the deck plate. Managers set priorities and own the schedule; junior technicians execute the routine work. You are the technical reference in between — the person who takes the hard diagnosis, decides the repair approach, verifies the quality of everyone else's work, and keeps operations moving when the answer is not in the manual. The ideal candidate has deep marine diesel experience, is credible across mechanical, electrical, and networked systems, and is comfortable working independently in remote, fast-moving environments with incomplete information.



Scope of the role

· Senior-level diagnosis, repair, and preventive maintenance across all supported platforms, CONUS and OCONUS

· Technical reference and quality standard for technicians at the assigned site or deployment

· Overhaul and rebuild support for diesel propulsion and associated systems

· Development and refinement of maintenance procedures, checklists, and troubleshooting guides based on field experience

· Mentorship, training, and quality verification for junior and mid-level technicians

· Field technical representation to engineers, operators, customers, and other stakeholders during operations and testing

How you support the mission

· Diagnose, repair, and troubleshoot diesel, mechanical, electrical, communications, networking, perception, sensor, power, and other integrated vehicle systems and subsystems.

· Perform inspections, preventive maintenance, repairs, component replacement, and system validation to return platforms to fully mission capable status.

· Execute complex diesel engine diagnostics, maintenance, and repair with high precision, and support overhaul and rebuild activities.

· Provide on-site technical leadership during field operations, testing, and customer events, coordinating effectively with technicians, engineers, operators, and customers.

· Clearly communicate equipment status, technical issues, risks, and recommended corrective actions to supervisors and stakeholders.

· Maintain accurate technical documentation, including maintenance records, troubleshooting notes, system configurations, test results, parts usage, and equipment deficiencies.

· Identify systemic quality issues and recurring failures, and recommend corrective actions to supervisors and the maintenance program.

· Proactively flag risks, parts shortfalls, or resource constraints before they impact operations or schedules.

· Travel approximately 80% of the time, including domestic and international assignments, to support field operations, testing, maintenance, and customer requirements.

How you support the team

· Set the quality standard on the shop floor and in field operations, and hold peers to that standard.

· Mentor and train personnel on equipment operation, troubleshooting, maintenance, and field procedures, and support quality verification for less experienced technicians.

· Develop and refine maintenance procedures, checklists, troubleshooting guides, and lessons learned so the team's knowledge outlives any single deployment.

· Serve as a key technical resource for cross-functional teams and field deployments, translating field realities into clear recommendations for engineering and leadership.

· Make informed decisions about complex maintenance workflows and repair approaches within your area, and communicate trade-offs to supervisors on challenging operational issues.

· Drive productivity within your area and take initiative to keep operations moving when issues arise.

· Support coverage of adjacent roles and help maintain operational continuity during staffing or scheduling gaps.

· Take full accountability for the quality, safety, and output of your assigned area or work scope, balancing thoroughness with urgency.

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer - Special Programs
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB OVERVIEW

Saronic Special Programs is a small path-finding team chartered to rapidly prototype new ideas. Special Programs is responsible for generating new ideas, building and testing physical prototypes, and validating future products which continue Saronic’s mission to redefine maritime superiority.



We are seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineer responsible for designing, building, and testing a variety of complex systems, including autonomous platforms and edge devices. You will work on a diverse range of technical challenges, including the design of assemblies, structures, linkages, and other electromechanical components. You will collaborate with a small group of like-minded developers to solve robust problems with limited resources and time. You will design in CAD and build in the shop. You will explore the frontier of maritime technology.

title: Cost Accounting Manager
text:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



Job Overview

We are seeking a Cost Accounting Manager to join our Accounting team supporting Saronic’s rapid growth. This role owns the core cost accounting processes, including standard costing, product costing, inventory valuation, and the cost accounting components of the month-end close. You will become an expert in our products, their manufacturing processes, and their costs, and ensure accurate, auditable financial reporting of inventory and cost of goods sold.

You will work closely with Manufacturing Finance, Supply Chain Finance, Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Inventory Control to ensure information flows cleanly between our systems and that inventory transactions are recorded and valued correctly. You will define the standards of excellence for cost accounting at Saronic and build processes that scale with the business.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys owning a function end to end, working side by side with production teams, and building resilient, controlled processes in a fast-moving, high-growth manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Own the standard costing process. Maintain cost accounting standards and standard costs for finished goods and production components in the ERP, including cost roll-ups that incorporate raw material standards from Supply Chain Finance and overhead rates from Manufacturing Finance.

 - Own inventory valuation. Own the inventory costing process and the related financial reporting impacts, including capitalization, absorption, and valuation in accordance with GAAP.

 - Own the cost accounting close. Own month-end close activities for inventory and cost accounting, including reconciliations, journal entries, reserves, and support schedules, and ensure accurate and timely reporting.

 - Analyze variances. Lead analysis of purchase price, usage, labor, overhead, and yield variances and other anomalies, and prepare clear explanations of discrepancies for senior management.

 - Ensure ERP integrity. Ensure the validity and accuracy of cost data and inventory records across PMS, MES, and ERP systems through analysis, internal audit, and coordination with Inventory Control, Production, and Manufacturing Engineering.

 - Partner with Manufacturing Finance and Supply Chain Finance. Coordinate on overhead pools and rates, raw material standard costs, and the financial impact of production and sourcing decisions.

 - Partner with production and operations. Work with Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Supply Chain teams to understand variances, resolve root causes, and improve how inventory transactions flow through the systems.

 - Define standards and controls. Define the standards of excellence for cost accounting, and design and implement controls and practices that prevent systemic issues and support audit readiness.

 - Drive process improvement and automation. Identify and execute improvements across production, cost accounting, and supply chain processes, and streamline and automate complex processes to improve accuracy and efficiency.

 - Support decision-making. Prepare financial analysis of manufacturing costs, inventory, and expense information to support leadership decisions.

 - Support audits and technical accounting. Support internal and external audits and apply sound technical accounting judgment to inventory and cost accounting matters.

 - Anticipate risks. Identify risks to cost accuracy and inventory valuation early, mobilize resources to address them, and make decisive calls in ambiguous situations.

Required Qualifications

 - 7-9 years of accounting experience, including significant cost accounting experience in a manufacturing environment

 - Hands-on experience with standard costing, including cost roll-ups, variance analysis, and inventory valuation

 - Strong grasp of GAAP and cost accounting principles for inventory and cost of goods sold, and of inventory management practices

 - Experience owning month-end close activities for inventory and cost accounting

 - Understanding of how data flows between production, manufacturing execution, and ERP systems (e.g., PMS, MES, and ERP)

 - Extremely strong Excel skills, especially advanced financial modeling and analytical techniques

 - Ability to streamline and automate complex processes

 - Excellent analytical skills with a strong focus on accuracy and attention to detail

 - Excellent communication skills and high confidence in stating professional opinions to cross-functional and senior stakeholders

 - Ability to work independently and under pressure in a fast-paced environment, prioritize against deadlines, and solve problems as they arise

 - NetSuite experience (preferred) or other accounting ERP experience

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance

Preferred Qualifications

 - CPA or CMA

 - Experience in high-growth, defense, aerospace, shipbuilding, robotics, or deep-tech manufacturing environments

 - Experience with low-volume, high-complexity, or program-based manufacturing and the transition from prototype to production costing

 - Experience with overhead absorption and overhead rate methodologies

 - Experience with standard costing

 - Experience supporting internal and external audits of inventory and cost accounting

title: Senior Customer Success Manager
text:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



As a Senior CSM at 1Password, you own and strategically manage a portfolio of customers – driving value realization, revenue retention, and expansion outcomes that consistently exceed expectations. You operate with full commercial autonomy: advancing expansion opportunities independently, engaging VP and C-suite stakeholders as a trusted advisor, and managing complex renewals without escalation. Beyond your own book, you raise the bar for the team through mentorship, playbook contributions, and peer enablement.



How we’re using AI today

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.



This is a remote opportunity within the UK.



Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.



What we're looking for:

 - 6+ years in a customer-facing, consultative, or technical role in SaaS – Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Technical Account Management, or IT/security leadership.

 - Demonstrated track record of exceeding retention, adoption, and expansion outcomes; experience recognized with performance distinction is a plus.

 - Proven ability to run executive business reviews with VP and C-suite stakeholders.

 - Background in cybersecurity, IAM, identity security, or enterprise IT preferred; former 1Password power user is a strong plus.

 - Strategic success planning and multi-threaded stakeholder management across a complex portfolio.

 - Commercial acumen: independently qualifies, advances, and documents expansion opportunities; manages negotiations without oversight.

 - Designs and applies AI-assisted workflows to commercial execution; documents use cases in a shareable format.

 - Strong Gainsight and Salesforce hygiene; consistent forecasting discipline.

 - Highly autonomous; manages complex accounts without requiring managerial direction.

 - Commercial thinker who connects customer outcomes to expansion potential naturally.

 - Strong executive presence – adapts messaging across technical, operational, and C-suite audiences.

 - Elevates teammates through knowledge sharing and informal mentorship.





What you can expect:


OWN AND GROW YOUR BOOK OF BUSINESS

 - Independently manage a portfolio of moderately to highly complex accounts – adapting success plans to each customer’s context without manager guidance.

 - Maintain full success plan coverage; produce documented best practices and playbooks, applied broadly across accounts with measurable KPI improvement.

 - Proactively identify and mitigate renewal risks; close risk CTAs with a high rate of success within defined timeframes.


DRIVE ADOPTION & VALUE REALIZATION

 - Achieve strong Executive Sponsor attendance in EBRs across segments; EBRs are value-driven, data-backed, and consistently advance renewal confidence.

 - Maintain commercial intelligence across strategic accounts – budget cycles, org changes, compliance mandates, and stack rationalization.

 - Translate advanced 1Password capabilities into clear outcomes for VP and C-suite stakeholders; tie adoption to measurable ROI and long-term advocacy.


LEAD REVENUE RETENTION & EXPANSION

 - Achieve strong amendment and renewal upsell win rates; proactively source and advance expansion opportunities with documented context.

 - Maintain forecasting hygiene with minimal blank or unmodified renewals approaching subscription end.


OPERATE WITH STRATEGIC RIGOR

 - Manage commercial objections, renewal negotiations, and competitive conversations independently – without escalation for standard to complex scenarios.

 - Build and present business cases to customer champions; advance deals with enough depth to move through the pipeline with AE alignment.


ACT AS A TRUSTED SECURITY ADVISOR

 - Deep working knowledge of the full 1Password product suite; design tailored success journeys connecting feature adoption to measurable business outcomes.

 - Incorporate regulatory context, breach patterns, and competitive dynamics into EBRs with confidence.

 - Design and share AI-assisted workflows with teammates in a replicable, documented format.


COLLABORATE & ENABLE

 - Lead joint account planning with your AE; cited by AEs as a proactive commercial collaborator who improves deal outcomes.

 - Mentor Level B CSMs through call shadowing, ad hoc coaching, or onboarding support.

 - Lead or co-lead cross-team initiatives; contribute tools or improvements adopted by peers.


MONTH 1 – ONBOARDING & FOUNDATION

 - Develop fluency in 1Password’s full product suite, CS methodology, and commercial motion.

 - By the end of Month 1, you will independently manage customer touchpoints and demonstrate clear understanding of renewal drivers across your portfolio.


MONTH 3 – PORTFOLIO OWNERSHIP

 - Full ownership of your book with consistent EBR cadence and expansion sourcing.

 - By Month 3, you are meeting key performance targets and expansion leads are flowing to Sales with documented context.


MONTH 6 – STRATEGIC IMPACT

 - Operating at full commercial autonomy; contributing to team practices and mentoring peers.

 - By Month 6, you are achieving top-tier customer satisfaction and recognized as a reliable commercial collaborator by your AE and cross-functional partners.



UK-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between £73,000 GBP and £106,000 GBP, and is commission-eligible. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, pension, and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.


Our approach to work
We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement.

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



The Developer Relations team builds developer tooling and creates awareness through events, social channels, and community activity. In this hands-on role, you’ll turn that attention into active users by owning the journey from first touch through signup, installation, first success, and continued engagement, while also owning the Developer Hub as the main conversion surface. By helping more developers discover and adopt 1Password’s developer tooling, you’ll contribute to the company’s mission and growth.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US. 



What we're looking for:

• 4+ years of experience in developer marketing, lifecycle or customer relationship management (CRM) marketing, or growth marketing for a technical or developer-facing product.

• Proven experience building lifecycle programs that improved activation and retention, with measurable results.

• Hands-on experience with marketing automation and lifecycle tools such as Customer.io http://Customer.io, HubSpot, Braze, or Iterable, as well as product analytics tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, or PostHog.

• Experience owning or substantially improving website conversion performance, including A/B testing.

• Strong writing skills, with an instinct for what developers find useful and credible.

• Comfort working with engineers and developer advocates and with technical concepts such as application programming interfaces (APIs), command-line interfaces (CLIs), software development kits (SDKs), and documentation. You do not need to be a developer, but you should be able to try the product yourself.

• Ability to work independently and communicate clearly in a remote, async-friendly team. Preferred: Experience with product-led growth, free-to-paid conversion, open source adoption, event and community programs, Structured Query Language (SQL), Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), scripting, search engine optimization (SEO), docs-led growth, or developer communities such as GitHub, Discord, Reddit, Hacker News, X, or LinkedIn.



What you can expect:

• Build capture-to-activation flows for leads from conferences, meetups, hackathons, webinars, and social channels, including QR codes, event-specific landing pages, follow-up sequences, and starter kits.

• Work with Developer Relations teammates so every event, talk, and social moment has a clear call to action, tracking, and post-event nurture plan.

• Turn social engagement, including launches, threads, demos, and community moments, into measurable traffic and signups through the right landing pages and offers.

• Design and run lifecycle programs across onboarding, activation, adoption, re-engagement, and expansion using email, in-product messaging, and community channels.

• Define activation for the product, build programs around milestones such as a first application programming interface (API) call, successful build, or integration, and segment messaging by behavior, role, language, technology stack, and source.

• Own the Developer Hub’s strategy, messaging, and conversion across its homepage, product pages, community pages, and events pages. Run continuous testing across copy, calls to action, page structure, and signup flows, and partner with Design, Engineering, and Documentation to improve time-to-first-value.

• Write or direct tutorials, quickstarts, sample applications, changelogs, and email content; build reporting from first touch through activation and retention; and share findings that help shape the roadmap and messaging. Early success will include auditing the funnel, launching event follow-up and onboarding programs, and improving signup-to-activation, event-to-user, and Developer Hub conversion.





USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $133,000 USD and $186,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $125,000 CAD and $175,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.


At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

Health and wellbeing
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy 

 Growth and future 
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

Community 
🤝 Paid volunteer days 
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
*Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.



You belong here.



1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.



Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs.



Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you.



Successful applicants will be required to complete a background check that may consist of prior employment verification, reference checks, education confirmation, criminal background, publicly available social media, credit history, or other information, as permitted by local law.



1Password uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies, including natural language processing and predictive analytics, to assist in the initial screening of employment applications and improve our recruitment process. See here https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf for the latest third party bias audit information. If you prefer not to have your application assessed using AI/ML features, you may opt out by completing this form https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/1password/automation-notice. For additional information see our Candidate Privacy Notice https://1password.com/files/candidate-privacy-notice.pdf.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
text:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re seeking someone to lead the future of fraud machine learning at Ramp. In this role, you will help build core machine learning models, design data architectures, and set strategic roadmaps to help Ramp mitigate fraud-related threats while minimizing the friction experience by legitimate users. You will partner closely with product and engineering counterparts across model design, implementation, execution, and analysis.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Employ statistical and machine learning techniques on large datasets to discover patterns of fraud, platform abuse, and identity theft

 - Prototype and productionize machine learning models and rules-based systems to protect Ramp and its users from fraud

 - Partner closely with Fraud Engineering and Data Platform teams to augment and leverage data across first and third party sources, ensuring we’ve added as much context as possible to every decision we make

 - Contribute to the culture of Ramp’s machine learning team by influencing processes, tools, and systems that will allow us to make better decisions in a scalable way




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Bachelor’s degree or above in Math, Economics, Physics, Computer Science, or other quantitative fields

 - A minimum of 5 years of industry experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist or Data Scientist

 - Strong python experience (numpy, pandas, sklearn, pytorch etc.) across ML techniques and backend engineering

 - Prior experience deploying Machine Learning models to production and making meaningful contribution to backend systems

 - Strong knowledge of SQL (Snowflake, Postgres, etc.)

 - Fluency with agentic (AI) tools for software development and data analysis

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, constantly improving, start-up environment that focuses on solving problems with iterative technical solutions




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - PhD in Math, Economics, Physics, Computer Science, or other quantitative fields

 - Context on Fraud and/or Identity Threat detection systems

 - Experience at a high-growth startup

 - Experience with the modern data stack ( Snowflake / Hex / dbt / RisingWave / etc )

 - Strong perspective on data science + ML engineering development cycle, especially in a post-AI setting

 - Experience developing LLM-backed systems or tools

title: Product Manager | Procurement
text:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

Buying something for a business should not require finance teams to piece together requests, purchase orders, receipts, and invoices across disconnected systems. Ramp is building a procurement experience that helps employees get what they need, gives finance teams control over commitments, and helps businesses pay for what they actually received.

As a Product Manager for Ramp’s Procurement offering, you will own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Ramp’s core procurement capabilities, including sourcing, requisition, approval workflows, renewals, purchase orders, receiving, two- and three-way matching, and inventory management. You will work with Engineering, Design, and Data to turn complex purchasing and accounting requirements into products that are easy to start using and reliable as customers grow.

AI creates an opportunity to rethink this work: build agentic buying experiences for employees, automate work for approvers and stakeholders, and businesses make better purchasing decisions. You will decide where automation can take work off a customer’s plate, where a direct workflow is faster, and where a person needs to review or approve an action. Success means customers get value quickly, adopt the product in their everyday work, and spend less time chasing information and correcting errors.

This role requires working in person at our NYC or SF office at least two days per week.

Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the strategy and roadmap for Ramp’s Procurement pod. Make clear choices about which customer problems to solve, how the capabilities fit together, and what to build next.

 - Build connected workflows across sourcing, requisition, approvals, renewals, purchase orders, receiving, invoice matching, and inventory management. Partner with Bill Pay, Accounting, and platform teams so purchasing records and decisions carry through to payment and customers’ ERP systems.

 - Spend time with finance teams, procurement leaders, purchasing operators, and employees. Turn observed friction into simpler experiences for first-time customers and powerful workflows for complex organizations.

 - Build AI-powered experiences that complete useful work, such as finding new vendors, managing a renewal, drafting a request from a contract, or helping resolve a receipt and invoice discrepancy. Prototype with customers and decide what should be automated, suggested, or handled through direct user controls.

 - Make automation dependable. Partner with Engineering and Data to define quality measures, test realistic customer scenarios, learn from corrections, and provide clear explanations, approval boundaries, audit trails, and recovery when something goes wrong.

 - Own outcomes beyond launch. Define and improve activation, repeat usage, time to complete purchasing work, and the accuracy of matching and exception resolution. Use data and customer research to choose the next iteration.

 - Lead execution with engineers and designers, make scope and sequencing tradeoffs, and align partner teams on dependencies. Work with Sales, Implementation, and Customer Experience to turn customer commitments into repeatable product capabilities and support successful adoption.




WHAT YOU NEED

 - At least three years of product management or equivalent product-building experience, with evidence of owning a product area from customer discovery through launch and measurable adoption.

 - Strong product judgment and systems thinking. You can simplify complex workflows while preserving the controls and flexibility customers need.

 - Hands-on AI fluency, demonstrated through products, prototypes, or meaningful projects. You can reason about model quality, latency, cost, and user control, and choose where AI improves the experience.

 - Technical and analytical fluency, developed through a technical or analytical degree or equivalent practical experience. You can work with engineers on data models and integrations, use data to investigate problems, and build prototypes to test ideas.

 - Deep customer curiosity and strong design judgment. You can learn unfamiliar purchasing and finance workflows, distinguish recurring needs from one-off requests, and make the product easier to use.

 - A track record of leading cross-functional teams, setting priorities, making difficult tradeoffs, and delivering outcomes through others.

 - Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a product direction, a complex workflow, and the reasoning behind a decision to technical and non-technical audiences.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with procurement, purchasing, inventory management, accounts payable, or accounting software, including purchase orders, receiving, matching, and exception handling.

 - Experience shipping AI-powered products used in production, including document understanding, agent workflows, and evaluation systems.

 - Experience with ERP integrations, multi-entity businesses, or enterprise approval and permission models.

 - Experience building products where accuracy and trust matter, with meaningful auditability, user controls, and recovery paths.

 - Experience at a high-growth startup, taking new products from initial concept to sustained use or scaling an existing product.

As a Customer Activation Manager at Ramp, you’ll help partner-sourced customers improve how they manage their finances. This role goes beyond getting customers live. You’ll work with finance leaders, their teams, and external partners to understand what needs to change, address resistance, and make sure customers see measurable value from Ramp. We’re looking for someone who’s led customers through change, is comfortable working with CFOs and Controllers, and uses AI regularly in their own work.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Guide partner-sourced customers from implementation through ongoing workflow adoption, with accountability for time to value and business outcomes.

 - Build a change management plan for each account: identify stakeholders, understand what’s slowing adoption, and help customer teams work through it.

 - Help CFOs and Controllers measure Ramp’s impact, including improvements in close cycles, spend visibility, variance reduction, and ROI.

 - Manage relationships across the customer’s organization, including finance leadership relationships you’ll own independently.

 - Use AI to prepare for calls, build customer materials, synthesize data, spot account risks, and reduce repetitive work.

 - Help customers evaluate and adopt Ramp’s agentic finance capabilities, including the changes these workflows require in their teams’ day-to-day work.

 - Work with Channel Partner Managers, Partner Consulting, Account Executives, and Technical Consulting to coordinate implementations and identify opportunities to expand Ramp’s use.

 - Share recurring customer needs, product gaps, and feedback with Product.
   
   


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - 5+ years in customer success, consulting, implementations, or a similar customer-facing role, with a consistent record of delivering customer outcomes and exceeding goals.

 - Experience driving workflow adoption and managing organizational change, including navigating stakeholder resistance. Finance or fintech experience is helpful but not required.

 - Regular, hands-on use of AI to prepare for calls, synthesize information, create customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks.

 - The ability to build a business case for workflow changes and explain their financial impact to CFOs and Controllers, connecting implementation progress to business results.

 - Enough technical depth to work with Product and Engineering on integrations, APIs, and workflow design, and explain those topics to customers.

 - Success in a fast-paced GTM environment, ideally at a SaaS or fintech company.

 - Strong collaboration skills and the ability to get work done across Sales, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams.
   
   


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience helping customers adopt AI-powered or agentic workflows, with an understanding of what gets in the way of adoption.

 - Familiarity with FP&A, accounting platforms such as NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, or Xero, expense management, or other finance workflows.

 - Measurable results in expansion, retention, or time to value.

 - Experience at a company where AI was central to the product or how the team worked.

 - Experience managing 25+ customers at once, prioritizing across accounts, and turning open-ended problems into clear plans.
